title: Hear a different word just by watching someone's lips
hook: Your eyes can trick your ears into hearing different words.

narration.text: Your eyes can trick your ears into hearing different words, it's called the McGurk effect.
When you hear a 'ba' sound but see lips forming a 'ga', your brain often hears 'da'.
This happens because your brain tries to combine conflicting sensory information.
It integrates what you see with what you hear to create a unified perception.
The visual input actually overrides or alters the auditory input.
You might experience this effect watching videos with poor audio-visual sync.
Or even in conversations, especially in noisy environments.
Have you ever noticed your brain playing these kinds of tricks on you?

description: Discover the fascinating McGurk effect and how your brain combines visual and auditory information. Learn why you might perceive a spoken word differently depending on what you are looking at.
topic: Why you might perceive a spoken word differently depending on what you are looking at, explaining the McGurk effect.
